translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylammonium Adhesive Patch
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in osteoarthritis (deformative arthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow, etc.), post-traumatic swelling and pain (bruises, contusions, sprains, etc.), and muscle pain.
translation.usage: Apply to the affected area once a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, if you have or have had aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), or if you are in the third trimester (late stage) of pregnancy. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol, if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy or possibly pregnant, having difficulty conceiving or undergoing fertility testing, a child, or elderly. Do not apply to skin with lesions (exudative dermatitis, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds, etc.), or to the eyes or mucous membranes. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are using loop diuretics (furosemide, etc.), thiazide diuretics, drugs that interfere with blood clotting (warfarin, etc.), antiplatelet agents (aspirin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Sometimes redness, rash, itching, dry skin, or irritation, or rarely swelling or anaphylactoid symptoms (hives, difficulty breathing, etc.) may occur. Applying where the epidermis is damaged may cause a temporary numb or stinging sensation; use with caution. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, or toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer, or perforation of the stomach or intestine occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from light.
